english: kill two birds with one stone

terms.latin: duōs parietēs dē eādem fidēliā dealbāre
evidence: Curius ap. Cic. Fam. 7.29.2 (Lewis & Short s.v. pariēs)
terms.comment: Literally “to whitewash two walls from the same pot”.

terms.latin: ūnō in saltū aprōs capere duōs
terms.gloss: to catch two boars in one thicket
evidence: Plaut. Cas. 476: jam ego ūnō in saltū lepidē aprōs capiam duōs
Lewis & Short s.v. aper: “to kill two birds with one stone”

phrases.latin: jam ego ūnō in saltū lepidē aprōs capiam duōs
phrases.english: now I shall neatly catch two boars in one thicket

sources: Lewis & Short: aper
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 256.
